# Blood-borne and sexually transmitted viruses

> *Viruses spread by blood, sexual contact or from mother to child, several of which establish lifelong infection.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Describe the group by its traits; explain one mechanism of harm for each main virus; recognise the enabling conditions that point to each |
| The group in one sentence | Viruses spread by blood, sexual contact or from mother to child, several of which establish lifelong infection. |
| Main viruses | HIV (anchor); hepatitis B virus; hepatitis C virus |
| Supporting viruses | Human papillomavirus |
| Later in the course | Liver, sexual health and haematology blocks; occupational exposure |
| Scenario questions | Most likely virus, with options restricted to the group; feedback names the discriminating clue |
